lineas.texto: Your fridge doesn't make cold. Not even a little bit.
It pulls the heat out of your food, and dumps it into your kitchen.
Here's the trick. A sealed pipe loop runs all around it, filled with a fluid called refrigerant.
First, the compressor squeezes that gas. And squeezed gas gets hot. Way hotter than your kitchen.
So it flows through the coils on the back, and gives that heat away to the room.
Then it's forced through a tiny tube. The pressure drops, and it turns ice cold.
Inside the walls, that cold fluid boils and soaks up the heat from your food.
Then it goes back to the compressor, and the loop runs again and again.
That's why the back of your fridge feels warm. That's your food's heat.
